definition.description: From a tall stationary stance in a clear, level, non-slip zone, lean forward as one aligned body until one recovery step is required. Recover with exactly one step, catch a stable split stance, and hold the terminal position before a controlled reset. Alternate intended lead legs. One repetition is one controlled lean, one recovery step, quiet split-stance catch, declared hold, and reset. This is not a sprint, multi-step falling catch, wall lean, reactive release, start test, or acceleration drill.

environment.space: one protected forward fall-and-catch zone with clear reset path and no cross traffic
inspection: surface traction, debris, moisture, and forward clearance
footwear, communication, exit, and coach sightline

can control a stable split stance and reset
understands exactly-one-step, no-sprint, stop signal, and exit rules
session balance, landing, lower-body, and technical-fatigue budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, head-first fall risk, repeated stumble, balance loss, unsafe zone, or communication conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal lean threshold, split stance geometry, hold duration, dose, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 98 and the focused falling-start collision packet: the exact one-step fall-to-catch ends in a held split stance and is distinct from Falling Start Sprint, support, cue, and multi-step forms.

anatomy.laterality: alternate intended recovery/lead leg across accepted attempts and record side-specific control
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, or guarantee acceleration transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate no-sprint initiation-control practice when the exact single-step catch, surface, and balance context fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Fall as one line, take one recovery step, freeze the split stance, then reset—do not sprint.
secondaryCues: do not break early at the waist
catch before a stumble but do not add a second step
expectedSensations: brief forward projection and one controlled catch
light split-stance lower-body and trunk effort
unexpectedSensations: pain, head-first fall feeling, knee collapse, stumble, dizziness, inability to hold, or repeated side difference

observationChecklist: aligned forward lean and exact one-step recovery
catch-zone surface, footwear, clearance, and reset
split stance, knee/hip/trunk organization, arm set, hold, side alternation, and first quality loss
accepted attempts, symptoms, rest, and side-specific control

faultCorrections.waist_break_or_early_step: reduce lean threshold and restore an aligned body-line fall
faultCorrections.extra_step_or_stumble: reduce lean, use slower rehearsal, or stop until a one-step catch returns
faultCorrections.knee_collapse_or_unstable_hold: reduce threshold or hold duration and restore split-stance control
faultCorrections.sprint_exit: restate the terminal hold and use another reviewed start task if acceleration is intended

doNotUseWhen: the intended task is Falling Start Sprint, multi-step catch, wall support, reactive cue, test, or acceleration work
catch zone, symptoms, single-step control, supervision, or communication is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved symptoms, unsafe conditions, repeated extra-step catches, or a mismatch between the requested task and the exact no-sprint hold contract.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to lean, step count, side, hold, support, cue, surface, dose, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, substitutions, and validation.

legacy.description: No-sprint forward fall, single-step catch, split-stance hold, and reset.
legacy.tempo: controlled aligned lean; one recovery step; quiet split-stance catch and declared hold
legacy.loadNote: Bodyweight single-step catch and split-stance hold; exact lean and hold are profile-specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate Falling Start Position Hold with exact no-sprint, one-step catch, hold, and side-accounting boundaries.
legacy.coachLanguage: Define the one-step catch and hold, inspect the zone, alternate sides, and stop before a stumble or sprint exit.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Lean, take one step, freeze the split stance, reset, and report symptoms.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact one-step catch, split-stance, surface, symptom, communication, and technical-fatigue context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: comfortable pain-free split-stance hold and reset
session balance and landing budget fit
stopSigns: pain, head-first fall risk, stumble, extra recovery step, knee collapse, balance loss, unsafe zone, or participant stop request
inability to hold the position or restore control with reduced threshold and rest
contraindications: symptom, unsafe surface, inadequate one-step catch or split-stance control, supervision, or communication
sprint, multi-step, supported, reactive, assessment, or acceleration intent without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute Falling Start Sprint, multi-step catch, wall hold, or reactive fall-to-hold work.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment from focused falling-start evidence; independent calibration remains required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact no-sprint falling-start catch-and-hold contract only.

variants.displayName: Forward Fall Single-Step Split-Stance Catch Hold

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate no-sprint forward-fall initiation-control and split-stance catch practice.

dosage.countRule: count only an aligned forward lean, exactly one recovery step, quiet stable split-stance catch, declared hold, and reset without sprint

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The athlete stays aligned into the lean, uses one controlled recovery step, catches quietly without collapse or extra step, holds the declared position, resets safely, and reports no stop symptom.
stopRules: stop for pain, head-first fall risk, stumble, extra step, knee collapse, loss of balance, unsafe zone, or participant request
stop when one-step catch or hold quality cannot be restored with a lower threshold and full rest
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Inspect the zone, declare lean/hold/side rules, demonstrate a one-step catch, observe from the side, balance lead sides, and stop before attempts become a sprint or fall drill.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Lean as one line, catch with one step, freeze the split stance for the hold, reset, and do not sprint away.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate initiation-control practice only; no guaranteed acceleration outcome is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: reduce lean threshold, hold duration, or attempts; extend rest; or use another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add sprint distance, cueing, support removal, extra steps, resistance, height, or fatigue density automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: One step, stable hold, no sprint.
supportPrompts.coach: The terminal hold—not acceleration—is the task.
